newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to close Telkom privatisation Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to close Telkom privatisation Wednesday.

text.p: South Africa will close its first major privatisation deal on Wednesday, leading to a $1.26 billion cash inflow from the U.S.-Malaysian consortium buying 30 percent of state utility Telkom, officials said.

Telkom is due to sign the equity partnership deal, agreed at the end of March, at 1500 GMT on Wednesday in Cape Town, after which there will be an exchange of cash for shares and a new board will take over management of the company.
U.S.-based SBC Communications Inc and Telekom Malaysia Bhd are acquiring the Telkom stake in the largest direct investment in South Africa to date.

Skme $260 million of the amount is expected to be used to retire state debt, but $1 billion will be deposited in Telkom's private sector bank account to help fund infrastructure growth -- a move that will impact directly on the money market.
Reserve Bank officials said the impact of this major inflow would be monitored closely but it was not yet clear on which day the money would enter the banking system.
"We will field the money as it comes in but we do not yet know exactly when that will be," said Andre Kok, general manager of the Reserve Bank's money and capital market division.

Given excessive private sector credit extension, rampant money supply growth and rising inflation, analysts believe the central bank is likely to drain most, if not all, of the proceeds through open market operations.
SBC-Malaysia Telekom have lost no time in taking management control of Telkom with several leading South African executives packing their bags to make way for the new team.
Telkom chairman Dikgang Moseneke said on Monday a new board of directors would assume their positions on May 15, the day after the closing of the deal.
The new board will consist of 15 members -- 10 appointed by the government (including two trade union representatives), three by SBC and two by Telekom Malaysia.

SBC's representatives on the board are John Atterbury, president and chief executive of international operations at SBC, Randall Stephenson, comptroller at SBC, and Russel McRae, president of SBC International.
Telekom Malaysia's board members are Nor Hizam Hashim, chief operating officer of the service company of Telekom Malaysia, and Nor Zainal Rahman, its company secretary.
Telkom's managing director Brian Clark quit on April 30 and a further three executives agreed last week to leave on May 31, including finance head Angus Bond.
I addition to the five board positions, 75 expatriate staff appointed by the U.S.-Malaysian group will take a hands-on role in managing the company.
